title: Termshow script (.termshow.yml)
description: Presentation layer for a `.termshow` recording: settings, chapters, cuts, annotations, highlights and snippets, plus optional `record`, `steps`, and `check` sections that describe a session to record and how to check it. Times are in seconds: `cuts` and `speed_map` use the recording's original timeline, and everything else uses the playback timeline (after cuts and speed changes).

source.description: Path to the recording this script belongs to. Informational: tools pair `NAME.termshow.yml` with `NAME.termshow` in the same directory.

chapters.description: Named points on the timeline, shown as markers and in the chapter bar.

cuts.description: Time ranges removed from playback. Applied at render time; the recording is not changed.

speed_map.description: Time ranges played at a different speed. Applied at render time, after cuts.

annotations.description: Text overlays shown at the edges of the viewport.

snippets.description: Copy buttons shown in the title bar for a time range.

steps.description: A session to type in a terminal, for `great-docs termshow record --steps`, which runs the steps and writes the recording. Ignored when rendering.

themeSpec.description: One theme: a built-in name, or a mapping that overrides parts of one.

base.description: Theme to start from (`default` when omitted).

cursor.description: Cursor block color (the foreground color when omitted).

palette.description: ANSI colors 0-15. With 8 colors, the 8 are reused for the bright variants.

settings.description: Render settings. Changing them needs a re-render, not a re-recording.

theme.description: Terminal colors: a built-in theme name, a mapping that overrides parts of one, or a light/dark pair (`auto` for the built-in pair, or `{light, dark}`). The player shows the side that matches the page's color mode.

font_family.description: CSS font-family list for terminal text.

line_height.description: Row height as a multiple of the font size. Around 1.2 makes box-drawing characters join up.

speed.description: Playback speed multiplier for the whole recording.

prompt.description: Replacement for the shell prompt character on prompt rows.

prompt_pattern.description: Regular expression that matches the prompt at the start of a row; used to find prompts when the recording has no input events.

type.description: Both types remove the range at render time; the editor previews `ellipsis` cuts with a brief … marker.

width.description: Maximum width: 25%, 50% or 75% of the viewport.

region.description: A rectangle of cells, 0-indexed from the top-left.

highlightTarget.description: The text to decorate. Give one of `region`, `lines` or `match`.

match.description: Regular expression matched against the screen text.

group.description: Capture group of `match` to decorate (0 is the whole match).

badge_text.description: Badge label, for the `badge-before` and `badge-after` styles.

pulse.description: Pulse the highlight's opacity while it's shown.

match.description: Regular expression matched against the screen text; the first capture group (or the whole match) is copied, falling back to `text`.

check.description: How `great-docs termshow check` compares a new run of the steps with the recording. Ignored when rendering.

ignore.description: Python regular expressions for text that changes from run to run, such as version numbers, dates, or temporary paths. Matching text is left out of the comparison.

record.description: How `great-docs termshow record --steps` runs the steps: the shell, the terminal size, and timing defaults. Ignored when rendering.

shell.description: Command that starts the shell, split into words the way a shell would (`bash --norc`).

cwd.description: Directory to start in, relative to the script file. Defaults to the script's directory.

env.description: Environment variables to set on top of the current environment.

typing_jitter.description: How much each typing delay varies at random, as a fraction of it. 0 types at an even pace.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for a prompt or a `wait_for` pattern before giving up.

prompt_pattern.description: Python regular expression that matches the shell's prompt on the cursor's line, so the recorder knows when the shell is ready for input. The default matches the `$ ` prompt the recorder sets.

keyName.description: A key to press: `enter`, `tab`, `backspace`, `escape`, `space`, `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `home`, `end`, `delete`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, or `ctrl+` or `alt+` and a letter.

step.description: One thing to do in the terminal: `enter`, `hide`, or `show` on its own, or a mapping with one action (`type`, `run`, `key`, `sleep`, `wait_for`, `marker`) and that action's options.

type.description: Text to type, one character at a time. Doesn't press Enter.

run.description: A command to type, followed by Enter. The step ends when the prompt comes back.

wait_for.description: Python regular expression to wait for on the cursor's line, or on the whole screen with `screen: true`.

marker.description: Label for a marker at this point. Markers become chapters when the script has no `chapters`.

delay.description: With `type`, `run`, or `key`: seconds between characters or key presses, in place of `record.typing_delay`.

count.description: With `key`: how many times to press it.

timeout.description: With `run` or `wait_for`: seconds to wait, in place of `record.timeout`.

screen.description: With `wait_for`: match the whole screen instead of the cursor's line.
